Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that there are multiple sub-questions present. To address your question directly:

The long-term results of the transanal pull-through (TAP) and transabdominal pull-through (TAP) surgeries seem to show varying outcomes. Specifically:

- TAP has been found to have significantly better continence scores, improved stool patterns, and reduced enterocolitis scores compared to TAP.
- The senior urologist was able to resect more tissue per time unit with less risk of secondary procedures due to incomplete resections in the lower group.
- However, there are no significant differences in complications between the two groups.

In summary, while both surgeries have their benefits and drawbacks, it seems that TAP has better long-term results regarding continence and other outcomes.
